product: GuideFinder, a Brilliant Directories member directory of outdoor guides and outfitters

m3.purpose: follow-up after scope v1 was approved

matching: A gold item matches an extracted requirement when every keyword group has at least one term (case-insensitive substring) in the requirement title or statement.

requirements.statement: Directory search can be filtered by activity type, region and certification level.
requirements.script: Marcus first says 'make search better, it is kind of useless'. Only after Sam probes does Dana explain customers want to filter by activity (kayaking, fly fishing, climbing), region and certification level.

requirements.statement: Customers can search for guides within a radius of a ZIP code.
requirements.script: Dana: people type their zip and want guides within 50 miles.

requirements.statement: Guide profiles show live booking availability from FareHarbor and Peek.
requirements.script: Marcus wants a live availability calendar pulled from FareHarbor and Peek on each guide profile, so customers can see open dates.

requirements.statement: New paid members are synced to HubSpot with their plan and region.
requirements.script: Dana: every new paying guide should land in HubSpot with plan and region so sales can follow up. Detail on fields comes in meeting 2.

requirements.statement: Members whose subscription payment fails are suspended automatically after a grace period.
requirements.script: Marcus asks for 'some custom code' that kicks out guides whose card fails, after maybe a week of grace. This is a built-in BD setting (Suspend Past Due); nobody in the meeting confirms that.

requirements.statement: About 1,200 guides are imported from the old WordPress directory CSV export.
requirements.script: Dana: we have about 1,200 guides in the old WordPress site, she can export a spreadsheet with name, email, region, activities and photo URL. Whether old reviews come over is never settled.

requirements.statement: Customers can leave star reviews on guides and an admin approves each review before it is published.
requirements.script: Marcus had a bad experience with fake reviews; Dana wants to approve every review first.

requirements.statement: Elite plan members appear first in search results.
requirements.script: Marcus: if you pay for Elite you should be at the top of results, that is the whole pitch.

requirements.statement: Guide profile pages load in under 3 seconds on mobile.
requirements.script: Dana mentions the current site takes forever on phones at trailheads with bad signal; Marcus: under three seconds on a phone, that is my bar.

requirements.statement: The homepage hero search widget is redesigned to match the new brand.
requirements.script: Marcus shares the new brand colours and wants the big search box on the homepage to look like the mockup.

requirements.statement: Profiles show a 'verified certification' badge that an admin grants after checking documents.
requirements.script: Dana checks guide certificates by hand; she wants a badge on the profile once she has verified them.

requirements.statement: A customer submits one trip inquiry and it is sent to up to three matching guides.
requirements.script: Marcus: a customer fills one form 'I want to fish the Madison in June' and the three best matching guides get it.

requirements.statement: Dana receives a weekly email report of new signups and revenue.
requirements.script: Said in passing near the end while people are wrapping up: 'oh, and I'd love a weekly email of who signed up and what we made, Monday mornings'.

requirements.statement: Three membership plans: Free, Pro at $29 per month and Elite at $79 per month, each billed monthly or annually.
requirements.script: Marcus first says monthly billing only, then a few minutes later: 'actually scratch that, guides keep asking for annual, do monthly and annual'.

requirements.statement: EU visitors see a cookie consent banner.
requirements.script: Dana: we get European visitors for Patagonia and Alps trips, our lawyer said we need a cookie banner.

requirements.statement: Guides can upload trip photo galleries, up to 20 photos on the Elite plan.
requirements.script: Meeting 2: Dana says photos sell trips; Elite guides get up to 20 photos.

requirements.statement: Logged-in customers can save favorite guides to their account.
requirements.script: Meeting 2: Marcus wants customers to 'heart' guides and come back later.

not_requirements.reason: reversed_decision: Marcus proposes it then says 'scratch that, forums turn into a mess'

modified.after: Only FareHarbor (Peek dropped), and a 'Book now' button that deep-links to the guide's FareHarbor page instead of live availability.
Elite rises to $99 per month and a quarterly billing option is added.
Target is now under 2.5 seconds on mobile and also covers the search results page.

removed.reason: Dana will use HubSpot dashboards instead.
Brand refresh postponed to next year; keep the default hero.

added.statement: Admins can export the member list with plan and renewal date to CSV for the board.

out_of_scope.statement: Guides get an SMS alert (via Twilio) when a new lead arrives.
A Spanish-language version of the site.
Guides can sell gift cards for trips.
